answer_text:
Let

\[
P_N=\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{(n^3+3n)^2}{n^6-64}.
\]

First factor the terms. We have

\[
n^3+3n=n(n^2+3)
\]

and

\[
n^6-64=(n^3-8)(n^3+8)=(n-2)(n+2)(n^2+2n+4)(n^2-2n+4).
\]

Also,

\[
n^2+2n+4=(n+1)^2+3,\qquad n^2-2n+4=(n-1)^2+3.
\]

Thus each factor can be written as

\[
\frac{(n^3+3n)^2}{n^6-64}
=
\frac{n^2(n^2+3)^2}{(n-2)(n+2)\bigl((n+1)^2+3\bigr)\bigl((n-1)^2+3\bigr)}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
P_N
=
\left(\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{n^2}{(n-2)(n+2)}\right)
\left(\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{(n^2+3)^2}{\bigl((n+1)^2+3\bigr)\bigl((n-1)^2+3\bigr)}\right).
\]

Evaluate the first product:

\[
\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{n^2}{(n-2)(n+2)}
=
\left(\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{n}{n-2}\right)
\left(\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{n}{n+2}\right).
\]

Now,

\[
\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{n}{n-2}
=
\frac{3\cdot 4\cdots N}{1\cdot 2\cdots (N-2)}
=
\frac{N(N-1)}{2},
\]

and

\[
\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{n}{n+2}
=
\frac{3\cdot 4\cdots N}{5\cdot 6\cdots (N+2)}
=
\frac{12}{(N+1)(N+2)}.
\]

Hence

\[
\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{n^2}{(n-2)(n+2)}
=
\frac{N(N-1)}{2}\cdot \frac{12}{(N+1)(N+2)}
=
\frac{6N(N-1)}{(N+1)(N+2)}.
\]

Now evaluate the second product:

\[
\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{(n^2+3)^2}{\bigl((n+1)^2+3\bigr)\bigl((n-1)^2+3\bigr)}
=
\left(\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{n^2+3}{(n+1)^2+3}\right)
\left(\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{n^2+3}{(n-1)^2+3}\right).
\]

The first factor telescopes:

\[
\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{n^2+3}{(n+1)^2+3}
=
\frac{3^2+3}{(N+1)^2+3}
=
\frac{12}{(N+1)^2+3}.
\]

The second factor also telescopes:

\[
\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{n^2+3}{(n-1)^2+3}
=
\frac{N^2+3}{2^2+3}
=
\frac{N^2+3}{7}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\prod_{n=3}^{N}\frac{(n^2+3)^2}{\bigl((n+1)^2+3\bigr)\bigl((n-1)^2+3\bigr)}
=
\frac{12(N^2+3)}{7\bigl((N+1)^2+3\bigr)}.
\]

Putting the two parts together,

\[
P_N
=
\frac{6N(N-1)}{(N+1)(N+2)}
\cdot
\frac{12(N^2+3)}{7\bigl((N+1)^2+3\bigr)}.
\]

Thus

\[
P_N
=
\frac{72}{7}\cdot
\frac{N(N-1)(N^2+3)}{(N+1)(N+2)\bigl((N+1)^2+3\bigr)}.
\]

Taking \(N\to\infty\), the rational factor tends to \(1\), so

\[
